title: How many CE hours do registered nurses need in California?
description: California BRN rules for RN renewal as at November 2026: 30 contact hours every two years, implicit bias content, first renewal exemption and records.
shortAnswer: Registered nurses in California must complete 30 contact hours of continuing education every two years, from providers recognized by the California Board of Registered Nursing (BRN), to renew an active license. Nurses certify compliance under penalty of perjury and keep certificates for four years for random audits. Newly licensed nurses are exempt at their first renewal except for a one hour implicit bias course, and approved courses with direct patient care content must cover implicit bias.
keyTakeaways: California Code of Regulations, title 16, section 1451(a) sets 30 hours of approved continuing education in the preceding renewal period as a renewal condition.
Nurses sign a statement under penalty of perjury at renewal and must keep certificates or grade slips for four years from course completion (section 1451(d)).

Since January 1, 2023, nurses in their first two years of licensure must complete one hour of implicit bias training even though the rest of the requirement is waived (Assembly Bill 1407, Business and Professions Code section 2811.5).
Since October 1, 2022, section 1456 requires approved courses to include implicit bias content unless they have no direct patient care component.
Nurse practitioners whose patients are more than 25% aged 65 or older must take at least 6 of the 30 hours in gerontology, dementia care or the care of older patients.
regulator: California Board of Registered Nursing (BRN), California Department of Consumer Affairs
appliesTo: Registered nurses holding an active California license
Nurse practitioners and other advanced practice certificate holders, who renew through the RN license
Hospitals, clinics, staffing agencies and continuing education providers that employ California RNs or offer them courses
Not nurses on inactive status, who may request an exemption

sections.heading: What is the continuing education requirement for California RNs?

blocks.text: As at November 2026, California RNs must complete 30 contact hours of approved continuing education during each two year renewal period, in addition to paying the renewal fee. The rule is [California Code of Regulations, title 16, section 1451](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/16-CCR-1451), which requires proof that "during the preceding renewal period or preceding two years, the licensee has started and successfully completed thirty (30) hours of continuing education approved by the Board."

The BRN's [continuing education for license renewal page](https://www.rn.ca.gov/licensees/ce-renewal.shtml) adds that courses must come from a continuing education provider recognized by the board, and that courses do not earn contact hours while the provider number is in expired status. The board advises nurses to check a provider's number in the BreEZe license verification system before enrolling.

The window depends on the license's status. For a normal renewal, hours must fall in the preceding renewal period. For a delinquent or lapsed license, or a move from inactive to active status, hours must fall in the preceding two years.

sections.heading: Do California nurses need implicit bias training?

blocks.text: Yes, in two ways. First, newly licensed nurses must complete a dedicated one hour course. The BRN states that under Assembly Bill 1407 (Burke, Chapter 445, Statutes of 2021), starting January 1, 2023, a licensee still within the first two years immediately following initial licensure "must complete one hour of direct participation in an implicit bias course" from a BRN approved provider, codified in Business and Professions Code section 2811.5.

Second, implicit bias content is built into approved courses generally. [Section 1456(a)(4)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/16-CCR-1456), amended with an operative date of October 1, 2022, requires every course to contain curriculum that includes the understanding of implicit bias under Business and Professions Code section 2736.5, unless the course is dedicated solely to research or other issues without a direct patient care component.

blocks.title: What this means for providers
blocks.text: A course with direct patient care content that lacks an implicit bias component does not meet section 1456 as amended. Employers that run in-house approved courses for California RNs should check each patient care course outline for that element.

sections.heading: Who is exempt from California RN continuing education?

blocks.text: Nurses renewing for the first time after passing the national licensing examination are exempt from the 30 hours, but not from the implicit bias hour. The BRN instructs these nurses to enter "EXEMPT" as the course name and "NCLEX" as the provider on the renewal form.

Other exemptions are available on request where the licensee is moving to inactive status, or can show the board that they have been employed or resident overseas for a year or more, practice outside California for a federal agency or the US military on a California license, or have had a hardship of a year or more, such as total disability of the licensee or of an immediate family member for whom they are responsible.

sections.heading: What course content counts toward the 30 hours?

blocks.text: Content counts if it is relevant to the practice of nursing, relates to the scientific knowledge or technical skills of nursing or to direct or indirect patient care, and enhances knowledge above the level required for licensure. Section 1456 also accepts courses in nursing administration, management, education and research, because they relate to indirect patient care.

items: **Accepted:** advanced pharmacology, advanced EKG and dysrhythmia, advanced IV therapy, patient monitoring equipment, certification or recertification skills such as Advanced Life Support, conversational foreign and sign languages, and courses in any specialty area of nursing practice.

**Not accepted:** self-improvement or attitude change, financial gain such as investments or resume writing, courses designed for lay people, unrelated liberal arts, employer orientation programs, and basic CPR, BLS, basic EKG and basic IV courses.
**Continuing medical education:** Category 1 CME is acceptable within the time frames.
**College courses:** 1 quarter unit equals 10 contact hours and 1 semester unit equals 15 contact hours, for courses above the level required for licensure.

blocks.text: There is no limit on the number of hours from independent or home study. A course with identical content and objectives taken twice in the same cycle counts only once, and section 1451(c) bars partial credit for a course.

sections.heading: Do nurse practitioners have extra continuing education requirements?

blocks.text: Some do. The BRN states that nurse practitioners who provide primary care to a patient population of which over 25% are 65 years of age or older must complete at least 6 of the 30 hours in gerontology, the special care needs of patients with dementia, or the care of older patients. These hours are part of the 30, not in addition to them.

Nurse practitioners who prescribe controlled substances and hold a DEA registration also carry the federal one-time 8 hour substance use disorder training described in [the DEA MATE Act requirement](/regulations/dea-mate-act-training-requirement).

sections.heading: What records must California nurses keep for a BRN audit?

blocks.text: Nurses must keep certificates, or grade slips from academic institutions, for four years from the date they complete each course, and must submit them when the board asks. Section 1451(b) makes the renewal statement a declaration under penalty of perjury, and the BRN says random audits are conducted regularly and every RN is subject to them.

Employers that track CE for their own credentialing should keep the same four year horizon. The general approach to [preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) applies: one record per course with provider number, date, hours and the certificate image.

blocks.text: Nurses who also hold a license in another state should check that state separately. Florida and Texas, for example, set different hours and mandatory topics, covered in [Florida nursing continuing education](/regulations/florida-nursing-continuing-education) and [Texas nursing continuing education](/regulations/texas-nursing-continuing-education).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry treats the implicit bias element in section 1456 as a content requirement on courses as well as a learner requirement, so each patient care course can show where that curriculum sits and which regulation it answers. Hours, provider numbers and retention dates attach to the nurse's record by rule. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Can California RNs complete all 30 hours online?
faqs.a: Yes. The BRN states there is no limit to the number of contact hours that can be completed through independent or home study courses, provided the provider is recognized by the board and its provider number is active when the course is taken.

faqs.q: Do hours from out of state courses count in California?
faqs.a: They can. The BRN accepts courses acceptable to another state's board of nursing and courses approved by American Nurses Credentialing Center approved accreditors when taken out of state. Courses offered inside California by out of state organizations must carry a BRN provider number.

faqs.q: Does basic life support certification count toward California CE?
faqs.a: No. The BRN lists CPR and BLS courses, basic EKG and dysrhythmia courses, and basic IV courses among content that is not acceptable. Advanced Life Support certification or recertification skills courses and instructor courses in CPR, BLS and ALS are accepted.

faqs.q: How long must California nurses keep CE certificates?
faqs.a: Four years from the date each course is completed, under section 1451(d). The certificates or grade slips must be produced if the board selects the nurse for an audit.
